Q1: Copper sulfate has a comprehensive hazard profile, with internationally recognized significant hazards (Tier 1) across several categories, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), oral hazards (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN). Additionally, it presents potential hazards identified through expanded scientific data and predictive models (Tier 2) for endocrine disruption (EDC) and inhalation hazards (IHL).
Q2: Copper sulfate is recognized on several prominent lists of concern. It is identified on the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor, and is also listed under the Clean Water Act and as a Pesticide Active Ingredient, highlighting its environmental and regulatory significance.
Q3: This chemical is very well characterized, supported by an extensive body of scientific literature with 91,000 references, significantly above the median for characterized chemicals. Its molecular formula is precisely defined, it is not classified as a poorly defined substance (UVCB), and there are no data deficient (Tier 4) hazard classifications, indicating a complete and robust hazard profile.
